headline: High: TREK’s collaborative MCP/browser surface can amplify Authelia-authenticated data exposure and workflow errors, while direct prompt-injection risk is limited by lack of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia has no browser or subprocess surface, so it is not a direct instruction sink. TREK does run browsers and use MCP, but the profiles do not show a shared channel or that Authelia outputs are ingested automatically. The only plausible bridge is unusual manual copy/paste or external orchestration, so the blast radius is small and uncertainty stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies TREK-generated text into Authelia admin inputs
IF a shared MCP server forwards TREK content into Authelia without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy/paste between TREK and Authelia admin sessions during review
Require provenance labels on any MCP-fed content
Use separate browser profiles for each agent
Review TREK prompts before forwarding them to Authelia

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and email addresses, while Authelia has broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces. Even without a documented shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive data from TREK into Authelia-authenticated flows or outbound requests in default collaborative use. The interaction is inferred, so confidence is moderate.
conditions: IF TREK exports reservations, MFA secrets, or API keys into an Authelia-protected workflow
IF Authelia forwards authenticated requests containing TREK user data to upstream services
mitigations: Restrict TREK to non-sensitive test data
Audit Authelia-forwarded headers and claims
Separate credentials for TREK and Authelia
Turn off any automatic export from TREK to external services
Mask secrets in logs and UI previews

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API/OIDC calls and TREK is collaborative with multiple instances and MCP, so both can contend over shared identity or session-backed resources if pointed at the same backend. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory, so I do not escalate to high; however, overlapping mutable auth/session state is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same OIDC or session-backed resource
IF TREK and Authelia are configured against the same mutable identity store
mitigations: Assign separate identity stores
Enable per-service namespaces for sessions and tokens
Test concurrent writes in a staging environment
Document ownership of each shared secret
Add locking around any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is described as a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as actionable. Authelia provides authentication and forwarding, which can let TREK-derived claims or recommendations influence downstream access decisions. Because the profiles do not show explicit verification gates, the pair has a default pathway for unverified output to cascade into action, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF TREK-generated recommendations are used as authoritative inputs to access or booking decisions
IF Authelia forwards TREK-derived claims without an independent verification step
mitigations: Require human review before acting on TREK outputs
Add a verification step before Authelia consumes TREK claims
Log source provenance for every downstream action
Block automatic execution of AI-generated recommendations
Use a staging tenant for end-to-end testing

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, email addresses, reservations, and logs, while Authelia is an authentication service with broad network egress and OIDC/ForwardAuth. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so I cannot claim high; but the pair clearly creates a compliance surface around secrets handling and logging/retention that is not documented as aligned.
conditions: IF TREK logs or exports MFA secrets, API keys, or confirmation numbers into Authelia-visible telemetry
IF the deployment stores EU personal data in a region not covered by the operator's policy
mitigations: Review retention settings for TREK logs
Exclude secrets from Authelia and TREK logs
Confirm data residency for any shared backend
Separate personal data from test data
Document a deletion/export workflow for both systems
